title: Weight/KV/Activation Budget Reckoner and Continuous-Batch Headroom Plan
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Serving clusters intermittently hit hard GPU memory pressure during mixed-priority continuous batching (short chat + long context). Current heuristics allocate a static fraction for weights + KV + activations which results in either wasted capacity (low throughput) or tail failures (OOM evictions of KV). Goal: Design and implement a budget reckoner — a compact runtime component and operator playbook that maintains a per-GPU memory ledger for weights, KV cache, and activation windows; enforces soft headroom corridors; and provides live admission and rebalancing signals to batching and offload subsystems. The reckoner should enable stricter SLOs for latency and reduce OOM-driven fallbacks by 50% for mixed workloads in canary clusters. Non-goals: changing model formats or kernel-level memory allocators (we'll interface with existing allocator hooks).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a per-GPU memory ledger with three tracked buckets: weights, KV-resident bytes, activation working set; values reported at 1s granularity
Continuous-batching admission uses reckoner signals: accept / queue / reject decisions and reduces OOM incidents in staging by >=50% vs baseline
Headroom policy implemented: soft corridor with dynamic lower/upper bounds driven by quantile of recent peak usage (90th/99th configurable)
A simulation harness demonstrates behavior across 10k synthetic traces (short/long mixes) and shows <1% tail OOMs under target thresholds
Documentation and operator runbook published (confluence link) with migration steps and rollback criteria
End-to-end canary rollout in cluster 'us-east-2-canary' completed and performance dashboard (latency/cost) shows <=5% regression in p95 latency for high-priority traces
discussions: 2026-03-01 - Asha Kapoor: Initial write-up and problem statement. Proposed a three-bucket ledger and subject to allocator hook availability.
2026-03-03 - Marina Chen (SRE): Telemetry cadence should be 1s to match current batching windows; suggested adding delta-based alerts to avoid noise.
2026-03-04 - Liam O'Neill: Prototype ledger implemented in branch; uses exporter to Prometheus and an in-memory fast-path for admission.
2026-03-05 - Performance Review: initial synthetic test shows improved stability but increased prefetch misses; decision to add conservative KV prefetch backoff.
2026-03-07 - Product Review (Ethan Morales): Acceptable as long as p95 latency stays within 10% for priority=high; asked for canary plan and rollback criteria.
2026-03-09 - Security (Priya Nair): No new secrets or KMS changes; suggested adding audit log entry for admission decisions for debugging.
decisions: Use a three-bucket ledger (weights immutable, KV dynamic, activations ephemeral) rather than fine-grained per-layer accounting to keep runtime cost low
Headroom calculated as dynamic corridor: lower = median_recent + safety_margin, upper = 99th_recent + burst_margin; margins configurable per deployment tier
Admission is conservative by default: prefer queueing over preemptive KV eviction for priority=high traces; eviction reserved for emergency conditions only
Expose a metrics bridge (Prometheus + tracing) and a userland API for operator override (no direct allocator change)
